recovery.title: Sessions that come back after a crash
recovery.body: If the computer freezes or restarts, Persisty relaunches the sessions, resumes Claude Code and shows what came back and what didn't.

projects.title: A place for every project
projects.body: Projects, workspaces inside them and sessions as tabs. The sidebar shows where an agent is waiting for you; ⌘1 to ⌘9 switch projects.

accounts.title: Several Claude Code accounts, no logging in and out
accounts.body: Connect as many accounts as you have. Persisty follows each one's 5-hour and weekly windows and opens every new session on the one with the most room.

states.title: You know which agent needs you
states.body: Working, waiting for you, asking for permission, stopped. The state comes from Claude Code's own hooks, not a guess at the screen.

pro.title: Line up the next request
pro.body: The queue delivers your request when the agent is free or the quota renews. Every request saves a restore point.

editor.title: Editor, git and notes in the same window
editor.body: Open the file the agent touched, read the diff, commit and jot down what's left without leaving the session.

privacy.title: Your code stays on your machine
privacy.body: Works without an account or internet. Code, terminal output and prompts never leave, and every outside call shows up in Settings › Privacy & network.

pricing.title: Start for free
pricing.body: The core is free and needs no account. Pro adds the queue, account rotation and restore points for {price} a month.

items.a: The core is: projects, workspaces, persistent sessions, recovery, agent states, editor, git and AI usage, with no account and no time limit. Pro costs US$ 9.90 a month and adds account rotation, the request queue, restore points, check on finish and a folder of its own per session.
Only for Pro and the team plans. The free plan works without an account and without internet.

items.q: Does my code go through your servers?
items.a: No. Code, terminal output and prompts stay on your machine. The app only reaches out to read Claude Code's quota, sign in and renew the licence, use the integrations and git remotes you connect, and look for new versions. Every call shows up in Settings › Privacy & network.

Claude Code has full support: states from hooks, resume after a restart and several accounts. Codex has sessions and states; its resume is not confirmed yet. Any other terminal program runs in a persistent session.

items.q: What happens if the computer restarts?
items.a: On launch, Persisty relaunches every session that can come back, resumes the Claude Code conversation where it stopped and shows a report of what came back, what failed and why. It never says something came back when it didn't.

items.q: Can I use several Claude accounts?
items.a: Persisty doesn't create accounts or touch limits. It uses the accounts you already have, such as your personal and your company's, through Claude Code's own sign-in, and picks which one opens each new session. Following each account's terms stays with you.

items.q: Does it run on Windows and Linux?
items.a: Persisty was born on macOS, where it is used every day. Windows and Linux builds exist but have not been tested on real machines yet; they will ship as a preview.
Yes. The free plan needs no network. Paid plans use a signed licence that stays valid for 14 days without a connection.

items.q: Which languages is the app in?
items.a: Portuguese and English. The website and the docs are also in Spanish.

Now. The Mac build is signed and notarised by Apple; the Windows and Linux builds ship as a preview, unsigned and not yet tested on real machines. Once installed, the app tells you when a new version is out.
